articles.summary: The BBC's Sarah Rainsford spoke to residents near the site of the overnight strike.
articles.body:

articles.title: Cafés especiais revelam sabores e aromas que vão além da xícara tradicional | G1
articles.standfirst: Com grãos de diversas regiões e perfis sensoriais, marcas como Lucca, Moka Clube e Distinto estão no Ítalo Barigui, ampliando as opções para quem aprecia bons cafés.
articles.summary: Com grãos de diversas regiões e perfis sensoriais, marcas como Lucca, Moka Clube e Distinto estão no Ítalo Barigui, ampliando as opções para quem aprecia bons cafés.
articles.body:
Durante muito tempo, encontrar um café com notas naturalmente adocicadas, aromas florais ou sabores que lembram frutas e chocolate era uma experiência mais restrita a cafeterias e lojas especializadas. Esse cenário vem mudando no Brasil.

Os cafés especiais ganharam espaço no mercado e passaram a chegar também às prateleiras dos supermercados, permitindo que mais consumidores descubram a diversidade de sabores e aromas que a bebida pode oferecer.

No Ítalo Barigui , em Curitiba, essa variedade está representada por marcas como Lucca Café, Moka Clube e Distinto , que reúnem grãos selecionados e diferentes propostas de apreciação.

A mudança acompanha uma transformação na maneira como o brasileiro consome café. Durante décadas, predominou no mercado um perfil de bebida marcado pela torra muito escura e pelo sabor intenso, que acabava tornando produtos de diferentes origens bastante semelhantes. Hoje, o cuidado com a seleção dos grãos e os processos de produção permite reconhecer características que antes passavam despercebidas.

A doçura natural, por exemplo, pode lembrar açúcar, mel ou caramelo, sem que seja necessário acrescentar açúcar à xícara. Também aparecem notas frutadas, florais, cítricas e achocolatadas, além de diferenças de corpo, acidez e finalização.

Essa diversidade começa na produção. A região de origem, o terroir, a variedade da planta, a altitude da lavoura, as condições de cultivo, a maturação dos frutos, a colheita e o processamento influenciam diretamente o resultado na xícara. São cuidados que permitem preservar a identidade de cada café e revelar características próprias de regiões produtoras como o Norte do Paraná, o Cerrado Mineiro, a Alta Mogiana e a Serra do Caparaó.

Com a presença dessas marcas no Ítalo Supermercados, o consumidor encontra diferentes perfis de cafés especiais sem precisar recorrer exclusivamente a estabelecimentos especializados. É uma oportunidade de experimentar novas origens, descobrir preferências e incorporar à rotina uma bebida que passou a ser apreciada com a mesma atenção dedicada a produtos como vinhos, queijos e azeites.

Café especial tem origem, identidade e personalidade

A principal diferença entre um café tradicional e um especial começa muito antes de a bebida chegar à xícara. Enquanto durante décadas o mercado brasileiro foi marcado por produtos de grande escala e torras muito intensas, que tendiam a uniformizar o perfil sensorial, a produção de cafés especiais trabalha para preservar e valorizar as características de cada lote.

Isso significa que dois cafés podem apresentar diferenças importantes mesmo quando são produzidos com a mesma espécie de grão. A altitude, o clima, o solo, a variedade da planta e o processamento após a colheita interferem no desenvolvimento dos sabores e aromas.

O Brasil reúne algumas das regiões produtoras mais reconhecidas pela diversidade de seus cafés. O Norte do Paraná, o Cerrado Mineiro, a Alta Mogiana, em São Paulo, e a Serra do Caparaó, entre Minas Gerais e Espírito Santo, são exemplos de terroirs com condições próprias de cultivo e produção.

Essa diversidade permite encontrar cafés com notas que lembram frutas vermelhas, frutas amarelas, flores, chocolate, caramelo e castanhas, entre outras possibilidades. São características sensoriais naturais do grão, e não necessariamente ingredientes adicionados à bebida.

Uma das descobertas mais interessantes para quem começa a experimentar cafés especiais é a percepção da doçura natural. Dependendo da origem e do processamento, o café pode apresentar uma sensação adocicada que lembra açúcar, mel ou caramelo, sem que seja necessário acrescentar açúcar à xícara.

A torra também tem papel fundamental. Quando realizada de maneira adequada ao perfil de cada grão, permite destacar suas características naturais. Já torras excessivamente escuras podem acentuar o amargor e encobrir nuances que diferenciam uma origem da outra.

A ilha de cafés especiais do Ítalo Barigui oferece atendimento de baristas e especialistas, uma experiência sensorial com aromas de diferentes grãos e degustações de cafés preparados em diversos métodos de extração. — Foto: Divulgação/Arquivo/Ítalo.

Do produtor à xícara, uma cadeia de cuidados

A valorização dos cafés especiais também mudou a maneira como o consumidor observa a produção. Informações que antes tinham pouca relevância na hora da compra passaram a fazer parte da escolha: quem produziu, de qual região vem o grão, em que altitude foi cultivado e como ocorreu a colheita.

Marcas especializadas trabalham com seleção de produtores e lotes, buscando identificar características específicas de cada safra. A colheita seletiva, por exemplo, permite priorizar frutos no ponto adequado de maturação, enquanto os diferentes métodos de processamento influenciam a maneira como os açúcares e outros componentes naturais se desenvolvem e se expressam na bebida.

É uma lógica que aproxima o café de outros produtos reconhecidos pela diversidade de origem, como vinhos, queijos e azeites. Assim como acontece nesses mercados, o terroir, o produtor e os métodos utilizados ajudam a construir a identidade de cada produto.

O resultado é uma bebida que deixa de ser apenas um acompanhamento do café da manhã ou do intervalo de trabalho. O café passa a ser apreciado também pelas particularidades de seu aroma, corpo, acidez, doçura e finalização.

Lucca Café leva a tradição curitibana dos cafés especiais ao Ítalo

Entre as marcas encontradas no Ítalo Barigui está o Lucca Café, uma das referências de Curitiba quando o assunto é café especial. Com uma trajetória iniciada em 2002, a marca construiu sua história a partir da seleção criteriosa de grãos, da torrefação própria e da valorização da produção brasileira.

O reconhecimento mais recente veio em 2026. O Lucca Cafés Especiais conquistou a quarta colocação no ranking The South America’s 100 Best Coffee Shops 2026 , sendo a cafeteria brasileira mais bem posicionada na lista. A seleção combina avaliação de um júri especializado e votação popular, considerando diferentes aspectos relacionados à qualidade do café e à experiência oferecida pelas cafeterias.

A história do Lucca também está ligada à difusão de uma cultura de apreciação do café que valoriza a origem e as características de cada lote. A proposta é permitir que o consumidor reconheça as diferenças entre os grãos e descubra novas possibilidades de preparo e degustação.

Moka Clube valoriza pequenos produtores e a diversidade dos grãos

Outra marca presente no Ítalo Barigui é a Moka Clube, que trabalha com uma seleção de cafés especiais e gourmet de diferentes produtores brasileiros. A escolha dos grãos considera a qualidade da produção e o cuidado dedicado a cada etapa, com atenção especial aos microprodutores.

Esse trabalho de curadoria permite reunir cafés com características distintas, respeitando as particularidades de cada origem. A seleção dos grãos e o acompanhamento do processo produtivo são fundamentais para preservar os atributos que tornam cada café diferente.

A proposta da Moka acompanha uma tendência importante do segmento: aproximar o consumidor da história por trás do produto. Em vez de oferecer apenas uma bebida padronizada, a marca valoriza a diversidade da produção nacional e as características que cada produtor consegue desenvolver em sua lavoura.

Para quem está conhecendo esse universo, essa variedade representa a oportunidade de experimentar cafés com diferentes intensidades, aromas e sensações, descobrindo preferências pessoais sem precisar ficar restrito a um único perfil de bebida.

No Ítalo Barigui o cliente conta com a opção de comprar o café em grãos da marca de sua preferência e levar moído para casa, serviço realizado todos os dias na Ilha de Cafés do Supermercado. — Foto: Divulgação.

Distinto amplia as possibilidades para apreciar café

A Distinto valoriza o trabalho do produtor da origem à torra. Fundada em Curitiba em 2014, a marca seleciona pessoalmente os lotes que compõem seu portfólio em visitas a sítios e fazendas parceiras. O contato direto com os produtores permite conhecer a origem dos grãos e o trabalho por trás de cada lote.

Na seleção, a marca considera o cuidado em todas as etapas, do cultivo e da colheita dos frutos ao processamento e à secagem. Esse olhar valoriza as escolhas de cada produtor e ajuda a identificar os lotes que melhor expressam as características de sua origem.

A Distinto trabalha exclusivamente com variedades da espécie Coffea arabica. Todos os lotes são classificados como cafés especiais, com pontuação acima de 80 pontos.

Em sua sede, o mestre de torras da Distinto aplica uma técnica diferenciada e ajusta o perfil de torra a cada lote. O objetivo é realçar a doçura natural, os aromas e os sabores que o produtor ajudou a construir desde a lavoura.

Uma nova maneira de escolher e apreciar café

A expansão dos cafés especiais no Brasil acompanha uma mudança no comportamento de consumo. O interesse por produtos com procedência conhecida, métodos de produção cuidadosos e características próprias tem levado mais pessoas a observar detalhes que antes passavam despercebidos na hora de comprar um pacote de café.

Também contribui para essa transformação a possibilidade de experimentar diferentes métodos de preparo, como espresso, coado e prensa francesa. Cada técnica pode destacar aspectos distintos do mesmo grão, modificando a percepção de aroma, corpo e sabor.

No Ítalo Barigui, a presença de Lucca Café, Moka Clube e Distinto acompanha esse movimento e oferece aos consumidores acesso a diferentes propostas de cafés especiais em um mesmo endereço.

Para quem já aprecia a bebida, é uma oportunidade de ampliar o repertório e conhecer novas origens. Para quem está começando, pode ser o primeiro passo para perceber que o café brasileiro tem muito mais diversidade do que aquela encontrada durante décadas nas versões tradicionais.

articles.title: Jensen Huang, ex-CEO da Nvidia, vai depor no Congresso dos EUA após caso com suposta espiã chinesa | G1
articles.standfirst: Jensen Huang terá que comparecer à Comissão de Bancos do Senado no dia 3 de dezembro. Convocação se soma ao pedido de três comissões da Câmara dos Representantes.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang terá que comparecer à Comissão de Bancos do Senado no dia 3 de dezembro. Convocação se soma ao pedido de três comissões da Câmara dos Representantes.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang, ex-CEO da Nvidia , gigante do setor de inteligência artificial (IA), vai atender à convocação do Congresso dos Estados Unidos e depor aos parlamentares. Ele foi chamado a explicar sua relação extraconjugal com uma suposta espiã chinesa, no caso que o levou a renunciar ao cargo.

A audiência está marcada para 1° de dezembro.

🖥️ A Nvidia enfrenta uma crise após suspeitas de espionagem envolvendo uma empresária investigada por supostos vínculos com a inteligência chinesa e seu relacionamento com Jensen Huang. O caso levantou questionamentos sobre a segurança de informações estratégicas da empresa.

O escândalo provocou a perda de quase meio trilhão de dólares do valor de mercado da Nvidia , despertou temores sobre a segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos e mergulhou a indústria de IA em um cenário de incerteza.

O pedido foi feito na quinta-feira passada (12) pelo senador republicano Tim Scott, que também solicitou o comparecimento do secretário do Comércio dos EUA, Howard Lutnick, na Comissão Bancária do Senado.

"Os relatos recentes provocam sérias preocupações sobre nossa segurança nacional e a proteção de tecnologias sensíveis dos Estados Unidos ", escreveu o senador republicano Tim Scott na rede social X.

A iniciativa se soma ao pedido de três comissões da Câmara dos Representantes para ouvir Huang, que completa 63 anos em 1º de dezembro, a portas fechadas, sob a ameaça de intimação judicial.

O fundador e CEO da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, conversa com jornalistas antes de uma reunião com o Comitê Bancário do Senado dos Estados Unidos, no Capitólio, em Washington, em 3 de dezembro de 2025. — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein / Reuters

Huang, casado há mais de 40 anos, reconheceu no domingo (15) um relacionamento extraconjugal.

Segundo a imprensa, ele mantinha um relacionamento com Alice Huang, ex-executiva da Megaspeed, uma empresa de centros de dados com sede em Singapura e que, de acordo com os serviços de inteligência dos Estados Unidos , trabalhava para o Ministério da Segurança do Estado chinês . Pequim rejeita as acusações.

Apesar do sobrenome, Alice Huang, cidadã chinesa , não tem qualquer parentesco com o ex-CEO da Nvidia .

Na quarta-feira, o jornal The New York Times revelou um segundo relacionamento extraconjugal com Kimberly Powell , vice-presidente da Nvidia para o setor médico.

Após o anúncio da renúncia de Huang na quinta, a Nvidia informou que a diretora financeira da empresa, C olette Kress, assumirá o cargo de maneira interina.

Sob a liderança de Jensen Huang, os processadores da Nvidia , inicialmente projetados para gráficos de videogames, viraram um componente essencial para treinar e executar sistemas de inteligência artificial.

Huang é o maior acionista individual da Nvidia , com uma participação de quase 3,6%, segundo a empresa.

O empresário também era um conselheiro informal do presidente Donald Trump para questões de IA e pressionava, há vários anos, o governo americano contra as restrições à venda para a China de chips avançados de IA por motivos de segurança nacional.

Pequim critica a política de restrição de vendas há muitos anos e, nesta sexta-feira, a porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores, Mao Ning, voltou a criticar "medidas de controle de exportações que perturbam a estabilidade das cadeias industriais e de suprimentos globais e não atendem aos interesses de nenhuma parte".

O caso é parte da disputa entre Estados Unidos e China pela hegemonia em uma indústria considerada a próxima revolução industrial e abalou o setor de IA.

A renúncia de Huang é "um dia sombrio para a Nvidia e para a indústria tecnológica americana", disse o analista Dan Ives, do banco de investimento Yorkville.

Questionado se o executivo deveria ter renunciado, Trump disse que dependeria das circunstâncias. "Se a mulher era uma espiã, sim. Se a mulher não era uma espiã, talvez fosse diferente", afirmou em uma entrevista.

"Falei com ele ontem. Ele está passando por um inferno. O que o faz se sentir pior é a esposa e a família", acrescentou.

A Megaspeed está sendo investigada pelo suposto desvio de chips de IA da Nvidia para a China, o que viola as restrições americanas à exportação que pretendem frear o desenvolvimento desta tecnologia por parte de Pequim.

As autoridades de Singapura, onde a Megaspeed tinha sua sede, anunciaram que proibiram o retorno de Alice Huang ao país em fevereiro porque ela não apresentou explicações suficientes sobre sua gestão na empresa. A executiva, no entanto, não é investigada por espionagem. A Malásia também anunciou uma investigação sobre uma filial da Megaspeed.

Nos Estados Unidos , vários congressistas, entre eles o líder democrata no Senado, Chuck Schumer, exigem explicações sobre o que o governo Trump sabia a respeito dos vínculos de Huang com a suposta espiã.

articles.title: Paciente recebe teste de Covid vencido em unidade de saúde de Vitória | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretaria Municipal de Saúde informou que lote foi revalidado pelo Ministério da Saúde e pode ser utilizado até 1º de maio de 2027. Paciente se submeteu ao exame no local, que apresentou resultado negativo.
articles.summary: Teste estava com a data de 1º de agosto. Segundo a prefeitura, o lote foi reavaliado pelo Ministério de Saúde.
articles.body:
Paciente recebe kit de teste de Covid vencido em unidade de saúde de Vitória, no espírito santo — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Uma moradora de Vitória recebeu um teste rápido de Covid-19 com a data de validade impressa vencida durante atendimento no Pronto Atendimento (PA) de São Pedro, na última terça-feira (10).

Apesar da data na embalagem, a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Vitória (Semus) informou que o produto pode ser utilizado porque o lote foi contemplado por uma autorização do Ministério da Saúde que prorrogou a validade até 1º de maio de 2027.

A paciente, que não quis se identificar, procurou atendimento após apresentar sintomas gripais. Dias antes, ela havia participado de um evento em São Paulo, onde outras pessoas também apresentaram sintomas semelhantes.

Segundo a moradora, enquanto aguardava para fazer o exame, recebeu um teste lacrado e percebeu que a embalagem indicava validade até 1º de agosto de 2026.

Ela contou que questionou um enfermeiro e recebeu outro teste com a mesma data impressa. Ao perguntar novamente sobre a validade, teria sido informada de que a data não interferia no resultado.

Mesmo apreensiva, a paciente se submeteu ao exame no local , que apresentou resultado negativo para Covid-19. Ela também relatou que outros pacientes atendidos na unidade naquele dia teriam recebido testes com a mesma data de validade.

Em nota, a Semus explicou que os testes rápidos são enviados pelo Ministério da Saúde e que o lote recebido pela paciente foi legalmente revalidado, com prazo de utilização estendido até 1º de maio de 2027.

A autorização contempla o lote 202503011, da marca Eco Teste, conforme documento apresentado pela Secretaria.

A Semus afirmou ainda que segue as normas estabelecidas pelos órgãos competentes e que atua com responsabilidade e rigor técnico para garantir a segurança da população.

A mulher contou que procurou o atendimento após apresentar sintomas gripais, sendo indicada a fazer o teste rápido para Covid-19. Dias antes, havia participado em um evento em São Paulo, onde pessoas com sintomas semelhantes se encontravam.

Ao perceber a data impressa na embalagem, a paciente disse ter questionado um enfermeiro, que lhe deu outro teste com a mesma data de validade.

Ao repetir a pergunta teria sido informada que a data não interferia no resultado. Mesmo apreensiva, a moradora realizou o teste.

Teste rápido para Covid-19 — Foto: Vinicius de Melo/GDF

Por que o teste pode ser utilizado mesmo após a validade?

Em nota, a Semus explicou que os testes rápidos são enviados pelo Ministério da Saúde e o lote apontado pela paciente encontra-se legalmente revalidado com a nova data de validade sendo 1° de maio de 2027, de acordo com o que determina o Ministério da Saúde.

A medida abrange o lote 202503011, da Eco Teste, conforme consta no documento emitido pela Secretaria.

A Semus afirma sua atuação pela responsabilidade, rigor técnico e pelo cumprimento das normas estabelecidas pelos órgãos competentes, assegurando a adequada condução dos serviços de saúde e a segurança da população.

*Este conteúdo foi produzido por Emanoele Gobbi, residente do 29º Curso de Residência em Jornalismo da Rede Gazeta, sob orientação da editora Juirana Nobres.

articles.title: 'Pessoas não serão mais necessárias', diz Riedel ao defender reforma | G1
articles.standfirst: Conforme o governador Eduardo Riedel (PP), a reforma administrativa prevê fusão de pastas, criação de secretarias e redução de cargos administrativos. Mudanças no secretariado serão definidas após discussão na Assembleia Legislativa.
articles.summary: A reforma administrativa em MS proposta por Eduardo Riedel prevê a fusão de pastas, divisão da segurança pública e redução de cargos para diminuir gastos estaduais.
articles.body:
O governador de Mato Grosso do Sul, Eduardo Riedel (PP), apresentou nesta terça-feira (17) uma proposta de reforma administrativa para 2027 que prevê a extinção de secretarias, a criação de novas pastas e a redução de pessoal em setores administrativos.

Segundo o governador, o objetivo é diminuir gastos e reorganizar os serviços públicos. As mudanças fazem parte de um pacote de projetos de lei que será analisado pela Assembleia Legislativa.

Entre as principais mudanças estão a extinção da Secretaria de Estado de Turismo, Esporte e Cultura (Setesc), a união das áreas de Cidadania e Assistência Social e a divisão da Secretaria de Estado de Justiça e Segurança Pública (Sejusp) em duas pastas. Com a reforma, o governo passará de 12 para 11 secretarias, além da Controladoria-Geral do Estado e da Procuradoria-Geral do Estado.

Segundo Riedel, a redução de pessoal busca diminuir gastos sem prejudicar os serviços públicos. O governador não informou quantos profissionais poderão ser desligados, nem quais cargos serão atingidos. Segundo ele, os servidores comissionados representam cerca de 3% do quadro de pessoal do governo, e cortes nesses cargos são feitos sempre que necessário.

"A Cidadania e a Sead, ambas as secretarias, têm área administrativa. Agora será só uma área administrativa. Certamente pessoas não serão mais necessárias nessa reestruturação", afirmou o governador.

O governador afirmou ainda que os gastos com pessoal representam pouco mais de 47% do orçamento estadual, acima do limite de 46,55% citado por ele. Com a redução dos gastos administrativos, o governo espera destinar mais recursos aos serviços públicos.

Governador Eduardo Riedel (PP) fez o anúncio do pacote de Projetos de Leis nesta terça-feira (17). — Foto: Mirian Machado/g1 MS

Extinção de secretarias e redistribuição de fundações

A Setesc será extinta, e as áreas de turismo, esporte e cultura passarão a ser vinculadas a outras secretarias.

A Fundação de Turismo de Mato Grosso do Sul (Fundtur) ficará vinculada à Secretaria de Estado de Meio Ambiente, Desenvolvimento, Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (Semadesc).

Já a Fundação de Cultura de Mato Grosso do Sul (FCMS) passará para a Casa Civil, enquanto a Fundação de Desporto e Lazer de Mato Grosso do Sul (Fundesporte) ficará ligada à Secretaria de Estado de Educação (SED).

Rodrigo Perez Ramos, secretário de Estado de Governo e Gestão Estratégica (SEGOV), explicou que a Fundtur ficará vinculada à Semadesc porque o turismo contribui para o desenvolvimento econômico, atrai visitantes e gera receita para o estado.

Segundo Riedel, a extinção da Setesc também permitirá reduzir estruturas administrativas duplicadas, já que as fundações têm autonomia para administrar seus recursos.

Segurança pública será dividida em duas secretarias

A Sejusp será dividida em duas secretarias: uma para a segurança pública e outra para os sistemas penitenciário e socioeducativo.

A nova Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SESP) ficará responsável pela Polícia Militar, Polícia Civil, Corpo de Bombeiros Militar, perícias oficiais e Departamento Estadual de Trânsito de Mato Grosso do Sul (Detran-MS).

Já a Secretaria de Administração dos Sistemas Penitenciário e Socioeducativo (Seapes) ficará responsável pela Polícia Penal, pela administração dos presídios e pelas medidas socioeducativas aplicadas a adolescentes em conflito com a lei.

Perez explicou que a divisão é discutida desde a transição de governo, em 2023. Na época, foram criadas estruturas separadas para administrar as áreas de Justiça e Segurança Pública. Agora, a proposta é transformá-las em secretarias independentes.

Cidadania será incorporada à Assistência Social

A Secretaria de Estado da Cidadania (SEC) será incorporada à Secretaria de Estado de Assistência Social e dos Direitos Humanos (Sead).

Com a mudança, a pasta passará a se chamar Secretaria de Estado de Assistência Social, Direitos Humanos e Cidadania, mantendo a sigla Sead.

Segundo Riedel, todas as subsecretarias serão mantidas. Já os setores administrativos serão unificados, o que poderá provocar cortes de pessoal.

"Quando a gente faz isso, a gente está garantindo a execução da política pública. Nós estamos eliminando gente da área-meio", ressaltou.

Fazenda, Governo e Infraestrutura também terão mudanças

A reforma também prevê mudanças nas secretarias de Fazenda, Governo e Infraestrutura.

A Secretaria de Estado de Fazenda (Sefaz) terá duas secretarias-executivas: uma de Administração Tributária e outra de Administração Financeira.

Já na Secretaria de Estado de Governo e Gestão Estratégica (Segov), a Secretaria-Executiva de Gestão Estratégica e Municipalismo passará a se chamar Secretaria-Executiva de Planejamento e Gestão Estratégica.

Segundo Perez, a mudança busca melhorar a integração entre o planejamento e a gestão financeira do governo.

As atividades de logística da Secretaria de Estado de Infraestrutura e Logística (Seilog) também serão transferidas para a Semadesc.

Com a reforma, Mato Grosso do Sul passará de 12 para 11 secretarias estaduais.

Administração dos Sistemas Penitenciário e Socioeducativo;

Assistência Social, Direitos Humanos e Cidadania;

Meio Ambiente, Desenvolvimento, Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação;

A Controladoria-Geral do Estado (CGE) e a Procuradoria-Geral do Estado (PGE) continuarão no primeiro escalão do governo.

Segundo Riedel, a reforma poderá colocar Mato Grosso do Sul entre os estados com menos secretarias do país. Ele afirmou que a redução da estrutura administrativa não deve prejudicar os serviços públicos.

A reforma começou a ser elaborada após as eleições, por um grupo de trabalho liderado pelo vice-governador José Carlos Barbosa, o Barbosinha (Republicanos), com a participação de secretários estaduais.

Riedel ainda não definiu se haverá troca de secretários. Segundo ele, qualquer mudança no comando das pastas será anunciada após a discussão dos projetos na Assembleia Legislativa.

articles.title: Kim Jong-un visita complexo turístico sob rumores de ida à China | G1
articles.standfirst: Visita ocorre em meio a especulações sobre encontro com Donald Trump e Vladimir Putin na China; imagens mostram Kim Jong-un acompanhado da filha, apontada como possível sucessora, em complexo turístico.
articles.summary: Kim Jong-un inspeciona obras com a filha Ju Ae sob rumores de reuniões com Donald Trump e Vladimir Putin durante cúpula na China.
articles.body:
O líder da Coreia do Norte , Kim Jong-un , inspecionou, nos últimos dias, as obras de uma zona turística próxima à fronteira com a China, informou nesta terça-feira (17) a agência estatal de notícias KCNA.

A visita ocorre em meio a especulações sobre uma viagem de Kim ao país vizinho, alimentadas por declarações de autoridades dos Estados Unidos e da Rússia.

Kim visitou a reconstrução do aeroporto de Samjiyon, uma linha ferroviária turística e uma estação de esqui no domingo (15) e na segunda-feira (16) . Segundo a KCNA, ele afirmou que os hotéis, alojamentos e residências do complexo estavam impecáveis e mereciam nota máxima.

A visita acontece em meio a novas especulações sobre uma possível viagem ao exterior do reservado líder norte-coreano, depois que o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou na segunda-feira que poderia se encontrar com Kim na China nesta semana.

Líder norte-coreano Kim Jong Un visitou uma zona turística em construção no norte do país, próximo à fronteira com a China. — Foto: KCNA via Reuters

A agência russa Interfax também citou o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, que afirmou que o presidente Vladimir Putin poderia se reunir com Kim caso o líder norte-coreano também participasse da cúpula desta semana da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (Apec), em Shenzhen.

Trump, Putin e o presidente da China, Xi Jinping, devem fazer um encontro trilateral histórico às margens da cúpula.

Fotografias divulgadas pela KCNA mostram Kim, acompanhado da filha, Ju Ae, visitando hotéis e inspecionando instalações próximas a uma encosta coberta de neve.

Vestida de branco, Ju Ae aparece esquiando montanha abaixo. A inteligência sul-coreana acredita que ela esteja sendo preparada para suceder o pai no poder.

Ao lado da filha, líder norte-coreano visitou instalações de hoteis e uma pista de esqui. — Foto: KCNA via Reuters

Kim determinou que a ampliação da pista do aeroporto siga os padrões da Organização da Aviação Civil Internacional (Oaci), informou a KCNA.

Ele também subiu o monte Paektu para avaliar uma estação de teleférico reconstruída e as obras nas proximidades do Lago do Paraíso. Segundo a agência estatal, Kim exigiu que todas as estruturas do local tivessem a mais alta qualidade.

Separadamente, Jo Yong Won, integrante do Presidium do Bureau Político e secretário do Comitê Central do Partido dos Trabalhadores da Coreia, partido governista norte-coreano, reuniu-se com Putin, segundo as agências de notícias russas Interfax e TASS.

Em um fórum realizado em Moscou na segunda-feira, Jo afirmou que o ambiente de segurança em torno da Coreia do Norte estava sendo levado a uma situação perigosa pela "política hostil inveterada" de Washington em relação a Pyongyang, segundo a KCNA.

Kim Jung-un inspeciona região turística. — Foto: KCNA via Reuters

O Ministério da Unificação da Coreia do Sul destacou na segunda-feira que a delegação norte-coreana, que estava na Rússia desde 14 de novembro, viajou pouco antes de uma cúpula entre Estados Unidos, China e Rússia prevista para esta semana no território chinês. O ministério afirmou que acompanharia os desdobramentos.

Enquanto isso, o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky, afirmou na segunda-feira que a Rússia estava recebendo novos carregamentos de "dezenas" de mísseis balísticos norte-coreanos todos os meses, citando um relatório de inteligência.

articles.title: Meta lança app de compra e venda de produtos usados no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Chamado de Achados, aplicativo reúne anúncios do Facebook e do Instagram, e está disponível apenas para Android. Brasil é o primeiro país a receber a novidade.
articles.summary: Chamado de Achados, aplicativo reúne anúncios do Facebook e do Instagram, e está disponível apenas para Android. Brasil é o primeiro país a receber a novidade.
articles.body:
Meta lança app de compra e venda de produtos usados no Brasil para concorrer com Enjoei — Foto: Divulgação/Meta

A Meta , dona do Instagram, do WhatsApp e do Facebook, lançou nesta terça-feira (17) um aplicativo de compra e venda de produtos usados para concorrer com o Enjoei. Chamado de Achados, o app é gratuito e chega primeiro ao Brasil.

Segundo a Meta, o Achados reúne em um só lugar os produtos à venda no Facebook Marketplace, nos grupos do Facebook e no Instagram.

O app está disponível apenas para Android . A Meta não informou quando lançará a versão para iPhone (iOS). Também não há um site dedicado ao Achados.

Os interessados podem conversar e negociar com os vendedores pelo aplicativo ou pelo WhatsApp, combinando diretamente o pagamento e a entrega. O Achados não processa os pagamentos, e a Meta afirma que não cobra comissão sobre as vendas.

Antes de negociar, também é possível consultar os perfis do vendedor no Facebook e no Instagram, além de avaliações, outros anúncios e seu histórico de vendas.

A Meta afirma que usa ferramentas automáticas para ajudar a detectar e remover golpes. Os usuários também podem denunciar anúncios ou vendedores caso identifiquem algo suspeito.

O app destaca diariamente produtos na tela de busca e na seção “Garimpo de hoje”, que fica no topo do feed. Já o “selo de achado” identifica anúncios selecionados a partir da comparação de preços com ofertas semelhantes no Facebook Marketplace.

Página para cadastrar produto no Achados, da Meta. — Foto: Divulgação/Meta

O investimento da Meta ocorre em um momento de alta no comércio de itens de segunda mão. Uma pesquisa da Confederação Nacional de Dirigentes Lojistas (CNDL) e do Serviço de Proteção ao Crédito (SPC Brasil) mostra que 46% dos consumidores que fizeram compras pela internet nos últimos 12 meses adquiriram algum produto usado online.

“O mercado de usados já tem uma demanda consolidada, mas, para crescer mais, ainda precisa de segurança, garantia e simplificação do processo de venda. Esse mercado deixou de ser um nicho, e o que move esse consumidor é o bolso: muitos querem economizar”, afirma ao g1 Daniel Sakamoto, gerente executivo da CNDL.

Ainda segundo o levantamento, os produtos de segunda mão mais pesquisados pelos brasileiros são roupas, calçados e eletrônicos, especialmente celulares, tablets e notebooks. Na sequência, aparecem móveis, eletrodomésticos, produtos para animais de estimação, brinquedos e jogos.

Segundo a pesquisa, Mercado Livre, OLX, Facebook Marketplace e Enjoei são, nessa ordem, as plataformas mais procuradas para comprar produtos usados.

articles.title: People's Palace in Glasgow secures further £10m in funding
articles.summary: The People's Palace and Winter Gardens on Glasgow Green shut for a revamp in April 2024.
articles.body:
One of Glasgow's most famous museums has secured a further £10m in funding for refurbishment ahead of its delayed reopening.

The People's Palace and Winter Gardens on Glasgow Green shut for a £35.9m revamp in April 2024 and was scheduled to reopen the next year, only for that to be postponed until the end of 2029.

The Category A listed building will now benefit from £10m of funding via the National Lottery Heritage Fund, with the money going towards a major restoration of the Winter Gardens glasshouse.

Before it shut, the museum struggled with structural and safety issues, including an enforced closure in December 2018.

The council said confirmation of the National Lottery grant meant nearly all the funding needed for the restoration has been secured, and the work would make the museum "more welcoming and inclusive".

The Heritage Fund said the redevelopment will secure the future of both buildings and help it "become a dynamic, community-led museum and flexible events space" in the long-term.

It said: "Visitors will enjoy exploring themes including politics and protest, culture and nightlife, and housing, health, and homelife.

"A dedicated new learning space will be created on the ground floor, while much-loved objects will return to display, including Ken Currie's paintings, the original Barrowland Ballroom signage and Billy Connolly's iconic banana boots ."

The museum first opened in 1898 to provide a cultural facility for working people in the east end of Glasgow.

Planned restoration work will also see improvements to accessibility and environmental sustainability.

Earlier this year Glasgow Life, the charity that runs the city's cultural attractions, said that the timeline for reopening the museum - as well as cost estimates for the work - were "continuing to evolve", delaying the previously announced 2027 date .

In September a report to councillors said December 2029 was being earmarked for the museum to open again.

That came on the heels of the Scottish government confirming £14m of investment to help with the rising refurbishment costs.

Eilish McGuinness, the chief executive of the National Lottery Heritage Fund, said: "The People's Palace and Winter Gardens belongs at the heart of Glasgow.

"This much-loved historic landmark will be reimagined for future generations and we are excited to support its transformation."

She added that the restoration would create an "inclusive, accessible and resilient place that celebrates Glasgow's people and stories.

"The People's Palace was built for the people, and it is the city's diverse communities who give it meaning."

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

Councillor Ricky Bell, the leader of Glasgow City Council, said the venue will be able to "welcome generations to come" once it is restored.

He added: "We are hugely grateful for this latest investment in the People's Palace and Winter Gardens, which means almost all of the funding for this landmark project is now secured.

"This restoration will breathe new life into one of Glasgow's most iconic civic spaces, creating a vibrant home for the stories, collections and communities that have shaped our city."

articles.title: Hospitality bosses in Channel Islands want closer partnership
articles.summary: A meeting has been held between hospitality leaders from Jersey, Guernsey, and the Isle of Man.
articles.body:
Guernsey, Jersey, and the Isle of Man should work together more closely to tackle their shared challenges, a hospitality leader has said.

Marcus Calvani, from the Jersey Hospitality Association, said the three Crown Dependencies had much in common they could promote and the Channel Islands could join with Brittany and Normandy to promote tourism in the region.

Representatives from the islands met for two days earlier this month at Longueville Manor in Jersey to compare how their visitor economies are organised and funded.

Calvani described the event as "inspiring and collaborative". The Multi-Island Visitor Economy Think-Tank has committed to meeting at least four times a year.

Among the subjects discussed was how to boost recognition of the "true value" of the visitor economy, and how to improve air and sea connectivity between the Channel Islands.

"All of our islands have the same kind of pillars, which are great food and drink, great history and heritage, and amazing outdoor areas for wellness, wellbeing and sport," said Calvani.

"So we started to look at whether we can take Jersey Food Festival and The Big Eat Guernsey, and how we could change it into an 'eating around the Channel Islands' event."

He added: "We could share data on who our customer is and what they like to do, and that could help us become more efficient and save costs."

The lead marketing officers from the States of Guernsey also praised the meeting.

"While each [island] has its own strengths and challenges, this meeting demonstrated the value of closer collaboration," said Zoe Gosling.

"Working together can help us make better use of resources, reduce costs and, most importantly, deliver a better product for our visitors across all the islands, which residents can also benefit from."

Calvani suggested a new digital platform for surveying visitors would be a better way of collecting feedback from their trips.

"It should create a more compelling case for groups like Visit Jersey, Visit Guernsey, and the government to fund bigger budgets in marketing.

"If we create great experiences for guests and visitors, we will also get great experiences as islanders."

articles.title: Channel 4 admits it doesn't know number of Married At First Sight UK sex abuse complaints
articles.summary: C4's chief executive is questioned by MPs after a string of allegations were made about the show.
articles.body:
Channel 4's chief executive has admitted she doesn't know how many complaints of sexual misconduct were received about Married at First Sight UK, despite a six-month external review into the hit TV show.

When asked by MPs, Priya Dogra said: "I'm not sure I have the details," adding that the review looked specifically at the claims of three women featured in a BBC Panorama.

Married at First Sight UK was cancelled after Panorama revealed rape allegations from two female cast members , while a third woman alleged a non-consensual sex act. The men involved have denied all the allegations.

Separately, Dogra said the broadcaster "cannot apologise enough" to a former employee who twice made complaints about Russell Brand and felt they weren't properly handled.

Dogra said it was "almost unforgivable" that the woman said she complained to Channel 4 in 2009 and again in 2023.

Brand is serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after recently being found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Married at First Sight UK, known as MAFS UK, had been running for 10 seasons and was one of Channel 4's biggest shows, with audience figures often topping three million.

The Panorama investigation in May heard from three women who made allegations about the men they were partnered with - claims the men deny:

One woman said her on-screen husband raped her and threatened her with an acid attack.

A second woman told both Channel 4 and production company CPL, before broadcast, about being allegedly raped by her on-screen husband. Her episodes were still aired.

A third woman accused her on-screen husband of sexual misconduct.

All three women accused the show of not doing enough to protect them.

A review was commissioned into MAFS UK by Channel 4 shortly after the BBC first contacted the broadcaster with details of the allegations.

Earlier this month, the completed review recommended extra safeguards on the show. But Channel 4 said the programme had "run its course" and apologised to the women involved in the investigation.

Speaking to MPs on the House of Commons culture and media committee on Tuesday, Dogra was repeatedly asked if she knew how many allegations Channel 4 and CPL had received over the years that MAFS UK was on air.

"I looked specifically into those instances [the three women], I did not do a broad sweep of every episode or every season of the show. That is not what the terms of reference for the show were," she responded.

"If there are others, we would take them seriously and look into them on the same basis."

"You're saying your inquiry didn't actually look at how many complaints were made into this show in total?" replied the committee's chair, Dame Caroline Dinenage.

"The inquiry looked at our handling of these specific incidents," responded Dogra.

When pushed about who would know how many allegations of harm had been received over the years, Dogra said that information would be held internally between Channel 4 and CPL.

Dogra, who started as Channel 4 chief executive earlier this year, also said she was "frankly uncomfortable" with some of the changes proposed by the review into MAFS UK - such as 24-hour CCTV and lockable bedrooms - hence her reason for axing the show.

Channel 4's bosses were also questioned at length about Brand by MPs in the hearing.

Brand's work on Channel 4 included hosting Big Brother sister show Big Brother's Big Mouth and its celebrity equivalent from 2004 to 2007, a chat show in 2006, and appearing on Big Fat Quiz of the Year.

Addressing Dogra and Channel 4's chairman Geoff Cooper, MPs said the member of staff who made two complaints about Brand "fell through the cracks".

In response, Dogra said: "I'm not sure we can apologise enough as an organisation for putting her through that twice. We have apologised in public in the past and in private."

She accepted that the woman's complaints were "not handled properly" and added that "it's almost unforgivable that happened twice".

When asked by the committee if junior members of staff could raise complaints against a star without fear of losing their job, Dogra replied she "can't say 100%" that that would be the case.

"What I can do is set the standard, set the tone, make sure that the facilities are available, make sure that my staff and the production companies understand the repercussions of not complying, and understand the kind of culture that I'm trying to set, and we're trying to set as an industry."

She also said she found the "cultural personality" around Brand "horrendous".

"I find it distasteful, and I look at the jokes... that is the lowest form of humour, because these are jokes that are made at the expense of someone else's physical safety.

"I don't believe it should have been acceptable then, and I certainly don't think it's acceptable now."

During the session, Dame Caroline also put to Channel 4 bosses that in both the MAFS UK and Brand cases, the broadcaster appeared like "a child with their hand in the cookie jar".

The committee chairwoman asked: "To what extent can you reassure us that Channel 4's priority is genuinely the welfare of the staff who work there, the staff who have worked there, and the people who take part in your shows - rather than purely when the world is looking at you and you suddenly feel that you've got a reputational reason to take a look at these shows?"

Dogra responded by saying that when Channel 4 commissioned the review, "we didn't even know whether the Panorama programme would be made".

She added: "We had received a right-to-reply letter and the programme came out six weeks later, but it equally it could not have been made. We always intended to do the review."

In the instance of the woman who tried to complain about Brand, she added: "I'm not sure there are more apologies we can give. Because none of those things should've happened."

articles.title: Welsh NHS given £500m boost in Plaid Cymru's first budget
articles.summary: Health spending will rise, but the government says it is grappling with "tight" public finances.
articles.body:
A funding boost for the NHS has been included in Plaid Cymru's first budget, but other public services could still feel the pinch.

Despite an extra £500m to cut waiting lists, spending on health will not rise as quickly as it has in recent years.

Money has also been set aside to negotiate a crucial political deal on the budget – the first since Plaid won power at May's Senedd election.

There are no changes to the rate of income tax that the Welsh government controls, nor to the land transaction tax that is paid by people buying properties.

With no overall majority in the Senedd, the party's Welsh government needs support from political opponents to approve its tax and spending plans.

Wales to make £100 energy payments but Plaid ministers say Budget leaves them with cuts

Reform UK continued its boycott of the Senedd for First Minister's Questions on Tuesday, as well as the budget statement that followed.

Announcing the budget in the Senedd, Finance Minister Elin Jones said the "public finances are tight" with the funding available to run day-to-day services expected to shrink 0.5% next year.

An extra £500m for health represents an increase of 2.1% after allowing for inflation - the rate at which costs are rising - but is well below the historical average rise of 3.6%.

Ministers have also pencilled in a real-terms cut of 0.3% on health spending in the following year.

Funding for local councils will increase by £176m, but some councils could see their funding rise by as little as 0.4% in real terms.

Council leaders have warned about a funding shortfall because of growing demand and inflation.

The government also wants to spend £75m next year and £111m the year after to expand childcare – a key manifesto commitment for Plaid.

But four government departments - local government, education, the economy and rural resilience - will have less to spend next year.

Referring to health and councils, Jones said providing "greater protection for these essential services" would have "consequences" for other parts of her £30bn budget.

Agencies relying on government funding will "inevitably face challenging settlements", she said.

Jones said: "This budget is a break with the past.

"It is a reset in how Wales spends public money, and it lays the foundations for everything this government wants to achieve over this Senedd term, including a stronger NHS, support for local councils and more help with childcare."

Winning the budget vote, due to happen next February, will be the biggest test Plaid has faced since forming a government.

Jones said she had a "sizeable pot", worth nearly £150m of day-to-day funding, to discuss with other parties.

She had already reached a deal with the Greens to fund electric car clubs and a climate resilience fund. But the two Green MSs will not be enough to pass the budget.

Most of the Welsh government's budget comes in a grant from Westminster, with around 20% coming from taxes set in Wales.

There was more money for Wales in UK Chancellor John Healey's recent budget, and the UK government has said funding would rise over three years

But Jones said the extra funding "did not offset the hit to our public services from higher inflation".

Capital spending, which pays for buildings and equipment, is likely to be 9.6% lower by 2030.

The agency that funds universities and post-16 education, Medr, is facing a below-inflation funding settlement to its £850m budget.

Labour pointed out the news came on the same day as a UK-government commissioned report by Alan Milburn into youth unemployment.

Jones said she accepted there was "pressure" on Medr's funding and there were "complex and important issues to address in relation to further education and higher education".

In the Senedd chamber, Jones and other parties criticised Reform UK for not being present to hear her budget statement.

The party continued its boycott of meetings in protest against a speaking ban for its Senedd member Joe Martin.

In a statement, Reform MS Cai Parry Jones said: "Whilst families continue to battle with the cost of living, their money is still being spent on overseas projects and more quangos rather than growing the Welsh economy."

There was a deal between Labour and Plaid to make in-year spending changes this month .

But Labour MS Huw Thomas said: "There is an awful lot in here that needs fixing based on what you are proposing and there will be an awful lot of people in Wales tonight worried for their services and indeed worried for their jobs."

Conservative MS Sam Rowlands called for the government to scrap land transaction tax, the Welsh equivalent of stamp duty, on people's main homes, saying the tax "punishes people for moving around on the housing ladder".

The Welsh Local Government Association (WLGA) warned about the prospect of job cuts, council tax rises and service cuts.

WLGA Leader Anthony Hunt, the Labour leader of Torfaen council, said: "I recognise it's not easy to set a budget in constrained financial times, but I would appeal to Welsh government and Senedd Members as a whole to put local services first."

articles.title: In Connecticut, a steamy take on America’s original sandwich
articles.summary: In central Connecticut, the tradition of steaming rather than grilling cheeseburgers endures in a handful of greasy spoons.
articles.body: At first glance, Ted’s Restaurant looks like any other old-school greasy spoon. A single-story storefront restaurant, situated close to the curb, with a long narrow counter and a few leather banquettes, plus the homespun smell of onions sizzling. But peer behind the counter of this central Connecticut spot, 18 miles south of Hartford, and the first thing you see isn’t the classic grill. Instead, you’ll find a series of stainless steel steaming cabinets that resemble vertical toaster ovens or windowless, metal-grey microwaves. These contraptions constitute the key element of Ted’s legendary cheeseburgers. It’s the region’s steamed cheeseburgers that set a handful of remaining local restaurants apart from your average diner or other mom-and-pop eatery. The steamed cheeseburger method is believed to have emerged at the turn of the 20th century in Meriden, where Ted’s is located, and in nearby Middletown, an era when various restaurateurs were experimenting with fast or mobile meals. The restaurants that have endured all retain the feel of the bygone era that birthed them and remain beloved by locals. “It’s underground, working-class food,” said Colin Caplan, a historian and tour guide who’s the author of “Pizza in New Haven.” “No one cared about the history of this food until all the industries closed.” The pride of central Connecticut The circa 1900 steamed cheeseburger tradition can be traced back to a place in Middletown called Jack’s, and migrated at some point to neighboring Meriden, according to Caplan, who studied ads from the era. Early vendors of these burgers sold them directly to workers in Meriden as they exited the factories where they worked. The burger represented a health trend; people believed steaming the burger reduced the fat content (and to some extent, it’s true because this cooking method doesn’t require any oil to cook and some of the fat is drained away). The niche nature of the steamed cheeseburger can be demonstrated by stopping someone on the street in nearby Hartford or New Haven to ask about the dish. Most likely, you will get blank looks. “It’s stayed in this central Connecticut pocket,” said Bill Foreman, the owner of Ted’s. New Haven, which is on the state’s southern coast, has its own claim to burger fame. Louis’ Lunch calls itself “the birthplace of the hamburger sandwich.” The restaurant doesn’t steam its burgers, but it does claim to have invented America’s signature sandwich in 1900. Not unlike Ted’s, Louis’ Lunch ushers customers back to an earlier time, with wooden booths and a menu that consists of a single item: the hamburger. And don’t ask for ketchup or mustard. “We stay true to our forefathers, so no condiments,” said owner Jeff Lassen, whose great-grandfather, Louis, started the business. While Louis’ Lunch broils its burgers rather than steaming them, it also uses a sui generis method. The burgers are cooked vertically over a gas fire in little wire baskets that are more than 120 years old. And no buns – they would get in the way of the taste of the meat, Lassen said, so sliced sandwich bread is used instead. “Sometimes you don’t need to tinker with it,” Lassen said of traditional cooking methods. Serving generations of factory workers Ted’s opened in 1959, and in the first decade of its existence, it would have been just one of a dozen or more restaurants serving steamed cheeseburgers in the Meriden area, Caplan said. The towns of Meriden and Middletown were once ground zero for this style of burger, and in addition to steamed cheeseburger restaurants, there were many other local restaurants that cooked hamburgers this way. What makes these cheeseburgers special? Well, steam, of course. “Steam makes it very tender,” said Trevor Robinson who owns K LaMay’s, another eatery about a mile from Ted’s and with a similar set up. Ted’s and its competitors also cook the meat and the cheese in separate steam cabinets, creating what one employee described as “a curtain of cheese” on the moist burgers. This culinary tradition has served generations of workers in the silver industry, at local lamp factories and in metal working concerns, persisting in a small corner of a small state even as much has changed. Today there are just a handful of places still fully dedicated to the steamed cheeseburger, including Ted’s and K LaMay’s, both in Meriden, and American Steamed Cheeseburger in the neighboring town of Wallingford. There are also a few other restaurants in central Connecticut upholding this culinary tradition by offering the burgers, but only as part of a longer menu of options. Other restaurants and burger chains use steaming as a step in the cooking process, but they don’t use the steam cabinets. Some of the old stalwarts that have disappeared in recent years were buried by the Covid pandemic, which claimed many mom-and-pop eateries across the US. In the 2017 edition of the roadside dining bible, “Road Food,” by Jane and Michael Stern, The Lunch Box was among the listings in Connecticut. The book also included O’Rourke’s, a beloved Middletown diner that would open each day long before dawn to feed truckers and shift workers, and served the steam cheeseburger. Now both are gone. “It’s humbling that we are one of the only ones left,” said Foreman of Ted’s. “Humbling because the community has supported us but in some ways sad, too.” An ‘ooey-gooey’ delight Foreman has owned Ted’s since 2007, but it’s hard for him to recall a time he wasn’t at the restaurant. That’s because it belonged to his uncle, Paul Duberek, and Foreman began working at Ted’s when he was 13. Duberek, for his part, took over the business from his father, Foreman said. Not much has changed inside the restaurant, even while the neighborhood around Ted’s has moved on. A mammoth, multi-bay carwash that faces it from across the street, for example, was certainly not there when Ted’s first opened. “We are the quintessential hole-in-the-wall restaurant,” said Foreman. The steam cabinets used by these restaurants, meanwhile, exist in a category of their own. Ted’s uses a proprietary model manufactured by a local metal shop. Inside there are metal racks like you’d find on a grill or in a normal oven where the tiny metal tubs filled with hamburger or cheese sit. The steam cabinets sit on an open gas range, not unlike an outdoor grill. “You can’t find them even at a commercial restaurant supply store,” he said. The staff can fit up to 48 hamburgers “in the box,” with the cheese going into the cabinet next door, where it becomes molten goodness. “It’s almost like fondue,” Foreman said, as he stood behind the counter. “It’s ooey gooey.” In fact, the cheese is such a star player in this food universe that burger-less steamed cheese sandwiches are on the menu – and popular. At American Steamed Cheeseburger, owner Tom Schappert ladled out the cheese for a customer’s burger one fall day, and as he worked, he said, “People who visit will look at the cheese and say, ‘What is that, butter?’” There are subtle differences between the steamed cheeseburger restaurants. At K Lamay’s, for example, Robinson uses a Wisconsin cheddar that’s been aged for four years. It renders the lava-like cheese soupier than Ted’s, for example, where the cheese remains firmer. The burgers are served on large rolls; K LaMay’s uses rolls from New Haven that are made by the venerable Lupi-Marchigiano Bakery. Some customization is available. At K LaMay’s, free toppings include lettuce, tomatoes, onions and pickles. Customers can also choose condiments such as ketchup, mustard and hot sauce. But if you want the traditional take, at Ted’s that means a steamed cheeseburger with mustard and onions, full stop. And although K LaMay’s offers chicken tenders, and a BLT is available at Ted’s while American Steamed Cheeseburger serves a signature “Fire Dog” hot dog dish, the main event for all three restaurants remains the steamed cheeseburger. ‘Somebody learned from somebody’ While the history of the hamburger at Louis’ Lunch has been documented, when it comes to the steamed cheeseburger, claims of who made it first can be murky, Caplan said. “Often there’s no record in history, you know, ‘I made this on Dec. 1, 1962,’” he said. And besides, he explained, with local eateries like Ted’s, “Somebody learned from somebody.” And that transfer of knowledge led to a new business. In the case of Ted’s, the current owner learned from his uncle. Ted’s also indirectly gave birth to K LaMay’s. Kevin LaMay was a longtime employee of Ted’s who struck out on his own. Robinson later bought the business from him. And Schappert said he grew up around the corner from Ted’s and worked with LaMay for many years. Ted’s has found success beyond the original location with a food truck that visits some of Connecticut’s most popular sports venues, including University of Connecticut football games. The truck can also be rented for corporate events. K LaMay’s, meanwhile, has been named to several best-of lists, including the Best Burger in Connecticut, according to Thrillist. And for its part, American Steamed Cheeseburger keeps late hours to serve the bar crowd, which devours the soft gooey mass of cheesy beef. Connecticut in the popular imagination is often personified by the state’s tonier precincts – Yalies in New Haven and the lavish summer homes of Litchfield County (often belonging to wealthy New Yorkers). The milieu inhabited by places like Ted’s is something different. In the towns where the steamed cheeseburger still provides comfort to local diners, an industrial vibe lingers, even as many of the manufacturers that created these industries deserted the region. Not far from Ted’s and K LaMay’s is a long four-lane, divided turnpike, lined with dozens of old motels, some erected in the 1950s at the height of car culture and before interstates such as Route 91 redirected traffic elsewhere. Not surprisingly, each steamed cheeseburger emporium is a portal into the land that time forgot and also a very personal, community space, harkening back to a pre-digital age before delivery apps (although all of the restaurants offer online ordering). At K LaMay’s, local newspaper clippings cover a plastic food service barrier, and posters commemorating major moments in Meriden’s history line the walls of the adjacent dining room. On the wall at Ted’s, for display, is an older, historic steam cabinet. At American Steamed Cheeseburger, inside the glass storefront display window are empty bottles from local soda makers, including Avery’s and Foxon Park, plus an old TV set. The narrow restaurant sits across from a vacuum repair shop, a half block from the train station; the sound of a train whistle occasionally bellows as customers wait for their burgers. It’s impossible not to describe all of the places as homey. And for generations of local customers, these restaurants have offered a taste of home – a taste of their hometowns. “Every time a restaurant from my childhood closes, a piece of my memory dies,” Caplan said. That makes anyone who loves central Connecticut’s steamed cheeseburger all the more determined to savor it and safeguard the tradition.

articles.title: What to expect during Tuesday’s nationwide FEMA emergency alert test
articles.summary: A nationwide emergency test is scheduled for Tuesday afternoon and is set to disrupt “normal programming” on televisions and radios across the country.
articles.body: A nationwide emergency test is scheduled for Tuesday afternoon and is set to disrupt “normal programming” on televisions and radios across the country. The test, from the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission, is routine, officials said, and is required by law. Yet it comes after a number of widespread outages affected online banking services, airlines and more in the last few days. Why exactly is the test taking place now, when can you expect it and what will it look and sound like? Here’s what to know. What is happening on Nov. 17? FEMA, along with the FCC, is slated to conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System. The Emergency Alert System from FEMA is a national public warning system made up of thousands of radio, TV, cable, satellite and wireline video providers, the agency said. Through the system, the president can address the American people or “share life-saving information with the public during a national emergency.” “During an emergency, every second is crucial,” FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton said in a news release. “FEMA’s alert and warning systems ensure that no second is wasted getting you the critical information needed to keep you safe.” The operational test will allow officials to “identify and fix potential issues before an actual emergency occurs,” Hamilton said. The test, officials said, is required by law and must take place at least once every three years. The last test was conducted on Oct. 4, 2023. In that test, the agencies also tested wireless emergency alerts, but those will not be part of this year’s test. Is the test related to recent outages? FEMA said the test is a “routine, scheduled test of the Emergency Alert System,” and it is not related to any recent outages. “It’s only a test,” FEMA said in a social media post Monday. “This is a routine check to ensure our public warning systems work when they are needed most.” At the same time, the agency acknowledged rumors swirling about the test’s timing. “We are aware of rumors, questions, and speculation about tomorrow’s test,” the agency said in a social media post Monday. “We love a good fan theory as much as anyone, but there is no secret emergency happening here.” The test comes days after several major outages led to widespread, hourslong disruptions across multiple business sectors. Last week, a worldwide Microsoft outage left Outlook and other apps unavailable for at least 24 hours. One day later, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop “citing extraordinary circumstances,” leaving travelers and planes stranded for hours. On Monday, JPMorgan Chase said a “software bug” led to problems with online banking services. Later in the day, a United Airlines outage stopped flights from taking off. It’s important to note, however, that “if an actual emergency or significant weather event occurs on test day, FEMA and the FCC may postpone the test.” Should that happen, the backup date is Dec. 3, 2026. What time will the test take place, and what will happen during it? The test is scheduled to take place at 1:20 p.m. CT on Tuesday. At that time, all radio and television broadcasters nationwide will interrupt normal programming to play a test message for roughly one minute. According to officials, the message will clearly state that it is part of a test. When the test is done, normal programming will resume. Unlike previous tests, this one will only air on television and radio, FEMA said. “Your cell phone will not beep, buzz or receive a notification.” What will the message say? The message will read: “This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. This is only a test. No action is required by the public.” Along with the test message will be EAS alert tones “to support accessibility for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.” The distinct and attention-grabbing sound of the EAS is intentionally loud and alarming. The audio signal used for the tests uses the same combination of tones familiar to Americans since 1963, when President John F. Kennedy established the original Emergency Broadcast System through an executive order. It’s also the same tone used in alerts sent by more than 1,700 local, state, territorial and tribal authorities that send similar alerts for more localized emergencies. Some broadcasters may choose to display the message in both English and Spanish. Do you need to do anything ahead of the test? According to FEMA, no.

articles.title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's ideas help you?
articles.summary: The government-backed report says its recommendations could help 440,000 young people into work by 2036.
articles.body:
Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".

In a major review, published on Tuesday, he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.

Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time. So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?

Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work

At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service. He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.

It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.

Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.

Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser. Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.

Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.

He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.

The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.

Alongside more work opportunities, Milburn wants a "major expansion" in further education for 18- to 24 year-olds, as well as more apprenticeship places.

Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.

Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.

He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.

If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.

Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.

By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.

The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis

At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report

Milburn has said he wants a fundamental transformation of how mental health support for young people is delivered.

Young people who are Neet should be guaranteed fast-track access to services within three months, according to his recommendations.

This would include things like vocational rehabilitation, talking therapies and counselling as part of a young person's plan with their local Youth Opportunity Service - which would be rolled out between 2027 and 2029 under the plans.

There has been a big rise in mental distress among children and young people in recent years, and Milburn's report comes at a time the NHS is facing huge pressures.

Milburn wants mental health support to be available for all young people digitally, without needing a diagnosis.

Some areas are already using these approaches, but scaling them up would be a major challenge and would take a long time to introduce across the board.

Plus, Milburn wants "fitness to work" notes to be taken out of the hands of GPs and put into community work and health teams, and for them to be "a trigger for help - not simply a certificate of absence".

Milburn wants these changes to begin in 2027 and would be linked to the Youth Opportunity Service rollout, which would be complete by 2029 under the plans.

More incentives for employers to hire young people

Milburn has said he wants companies to be incentivised to employ more young people, with the report highlighting a competitive jobs market and applicants who often fail to hear back from potential employers.

The report includes three asks of employers: to create more genuine first jobs, more first-job apprenticeships and much wider access to meaningful work experience.

Plus, Milburn wants large employers to find ways of responding to rejected job applicants.

These changes should be felt by both employers and the young people looking for jobs by 2029, the report says.

To achieve this, the report suggests a £3,000 payment for employers who take on someone who has been Neet for six months, with a further premium of £2,000 available if they are a small business.

An extra payment of £2,000 would go to employers taking on somebody taking substantially greater barriers, such as care leavers or disabled young people.

These payments are proposed to be part of changes to the Youth Jobs Grant - which already exists - but they would expand under Milburn's proposals from 2027.

articles.title: In 1981, British builders lowered a prefabricated upper floor onto a house by crane, making it watertight in just a week; 45 years later, the experimental three-bedroom home goes on sale for £500,000
articles.summary: A three-bedroom house known as ‘Topper’ on Bradwell Common in Milton Keynes has hit the market with an asking price of £500,000.
articles.body: A three-bedroom house known as ‘Topper’ on Bradwell Common in Milton Keynes has hit the market with an asking price of £500,000. Its ground floor was cast on site, while the upper storey was built elsewhere and lifted into place by crane. From bare slab to watertight shell, it took about a week. The house was built for Homeworld ’81, a housing exhibition held in May 1981. Designed by Griffiths Keyworth and Associates, the house was built by construction giant John Mowlem. It is one of 36 homes designed to showcase new ways of building houses. The house’s nickname, Topper, comes from the crane-lowered upper floor.The exhibition wasn’t an accident. Back in the day, energy prices had risen sharply after the oil crises of the 1970s. British housebuilding had slumped. Milton Keynes Development Corporation invited developers from Britain and abroad to try new approaches. They wanted faster construction, smaller plots, solar power, better insulation and alternative materials. Though most of these ideas may look ordinary now, that was not the case back then. In 1981, double glazing, draught-proofing and sophisticated thermostats were far from standard in most homes.While most exhibition homes were built to be knocked down once the crowds went home, these weren’t. Every house was sold after the exhibition closed, and none was demolished. Many are still standing today. Homeworld was also the first of three major housing exhibitions in Milton Keynes. Energy World followed in 1986, and Futureworld in 1994.Inside the ‘home of the future’The freehold property has 1,302 square feet of living space. The house has three bedrooms, three reception rooms, a kitchen and a four-piece bathroom. Outside, there is a wraparound garden, a driveway and a single garage. The sellers have owned the property for more than 30 years. They have decided to offload it as they are now relocating. The listing describes it as rare to market, which is hard to dispute.The house sits near Milton Keynes Central station. The fastest trains reach London Euston in about 32 minutes, though the average journey is closer to 45 minutes. The A5 provides road access for drivers. Viewings are by appointment through Alexander Lawrence. Interested buyers need to register in advance to arrange a tour and discuss the property further.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision?
